faq.q: What does Pinnacle’s 2.7 billion+ data-point figure mean?
faq.a: The September 2026 company handout reports 2.7 billion+ structured platform records, based on database rows/events with a 17 July 2026 cutoff. Examples include session entries, assessment observations and technique ratings. The number is not a count of unique children, independent trial observations or verified AI-training examples.

faq.q: Does this establish the world’s largest child-development dataset?
faq.a: No comparable worldwide ranking is established. For example, CentralReach reports over 5 billion clinical and financial data points, using a different counting basis. A valid comparison would need common definitions, dates, populations, data quality and permitted uses.

faq.q: Does the MD-5 licence approve the entire child-development lifecycle?
faq.a: The MD-5 names PinnacleAI GPT-OS v1.0.0 and defined non-diagnostic functions for ages 0–12. The broader BIS schedule lists software processes and developmental-support modules across the journey. These instruments establish different scopes; neither guarantees outcomes or certifies global exclusivity.

faq.q: Do WHO, UNICEF, CDC, NICE or UNESCO endorse Pinnacle?
faq.a: No endorsement is established by the references on this page. Their guidance explains why monitoring, coordinated support, caregiver participation and inclusion matter. Pinnacle’s own documents must separately establish what Pinnacle provides.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Pinnacle developmental pathway?
faq.a: Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs. Its tagline is “Every child deserves a wonderful life.” The described approach connects ability measurement, child-specific planning, coordinated intervention, everyday practice, tracking, correction and reassessment. Individual outcomes vary.

faq.q: What do 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills mean?
faq.a: Pinnacle describes these as different layers of its developmental framework: 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, with 591 observations and AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. The totals belong to Pinnacle’s architecture, not a WHO-defined numerical hierarchy. Individual plans select relevant priorities. The earlier Whitebook used 344 skills across six domains; validation of an earlier version should not be automatically transferred to the newer framework.

faq.q: How do daily practice and monthly review connect?
faq.a: The company sources describe 7–9 daily techniques selected for the child’s programme, human feedback through the Fusion tracking and correction module, and monthly AbilityScore refresh. The care team should explain the child-specific goals, practice guidance, review schedule and any adjustments. This is a programme description, not a guaranteed outcome.

faq.q: How do ICD-11, ICF, ICHI and SNOMED CT relate to PinnacleAI?
faq.a: Pinnacle’s dossier describes architecture and mappings using WHO’s ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT terminology from SNOMED International. Their roles are health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and consistent clinical meaning. Correct implementation can support interoperability; an item-by-item mapping audit was not supplied. Alignment is separate from endorsement, clinical validation and the licensed device’s intended use.

faq.q: Does Pinnacle focus on a diagnosis or on everyday-life goals?
faq.a: Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need. These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

faq.q: Is PinnacleAI certified as sovereign-grade or authorised worldwide?
faq.a: The reviewed documents do not establish a sovereign-grade certification or worldwide market authorisation. Pinnacle describes an architecture intended for population-scale developmental support. A specific deployment needs documented local control and governance, validated interoperability, applicable permissions, operational capacity and evidence of performance for that population. MD-5 and BIS provide the particular scopes shown in their records.

faq.q: Are parents and caregivers named in the MD-5 intended use?
faq.a: Yes. The MD-5 annexure states that PinnacleAI GPT-OS is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators and caregivers through developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support for ages 0–12. This explicitly includes family users of the licensed software. It does not confer professional therapist credentials or register homes as therapy centres; worldwide exclusivity has not been established.

familyMeaning.md5: A defined intended use lets your family understand what the software is designed to support and when professional clinical evaluation is needed.
familyMeaning.bis: A documented software lifecycle makes quality responsibilities and the scope of developmental-support modules easier to examine.
familyMeaning.lei: A matching legal identity helps you trace the organisation behind a credential or agreement.
familyMeaning.classification: Reading the application and issued licence together helps you distinguish a requested classification from the device’s licensed classification.
familyMeaning.md3: The application explains part of the regulatory journey; the issued licence is the document to use for the resulting permission.
familyMeaning.iso13485: Quality-management evidence helps you ask how software development, changes and corrective action are controlled.
familyMeaning.iso27001: Information-security evidence helps you ask how sensitive developmental information is managed within the certified scope.
familyMeaning.mca: A documented name history connects today’s organisation with credentials issued under earlier names.
familyMeaning.dpiit: Startup recognition explains a business credential. Your child’s care plan should be evaluated using its own clinical and service evidence.
familyMeaning.udyam: Enterprise registration makes the business identity and classification traceable.
familyMeaning.gst: The printed legal and trade names help families and institutions match the supplier on invoices and records.
familyMeaning.pan: The inspected corporate identity document adds an identity check while keeping the tax identifier out of public display.
familyMeaning.hfr: A facility identifier gives you a specific record to ask about when checking the centre your family will visit.
familyMeaning.district-register: District summaries help locate relevant institution documents; match the individual certificate to the exact premises.
familyMeaning.rpwd-attapur: This document gives families an institution-specific registration to match against the address and service being considered.
familyMeaning.rpwd-begumpet: This document gives families an institution-specific registration to match against the address and service being considered.
familyMeaning.rpwd-nizamabad: This document gives families an institution-specific registration to match against the address and service being considered.
familyMeaning.rpwd-nellore: The historical record makes the earlier registration period traceable and identifies the renewal needed to establish current coverage.
familyMeaning.sae3000: A clearly defined assurance scope helps you distinguish institutional-record checks from evidence about a child’s clinical outcome.
familyMeaning.srs4400: Specified factual checks make the counting method more understandable; they do not supply an assurance opinion on outcomes.
familyMeaning.operating-metrics: Consistent records can support continuity across a child’s journey. Ask to see your child’s own goals and progress reviews alongside network-level numbers.
familyMeaning.methodology: A methods paper lets practitioners examine how a measurement approach was developed and where further validation is needed.
familyMeaning.external-validation: A published protocol makes the proposed research question and methods visible before a completed result is claimed.
familyMeaning.study-portfolio: Study-level detail helps families and referring professionals see which children and outcomes a research statement actually concerns.
familyMeaning.outcome-claim: Your child’s goals, starting point and reassessments make progress meaningful; a network headline cannot predict an individual result.
familyMeaning.appreciations: Original letters let you understand who acknowledged which contribution and in what context.
familyMeaning.awards: Distinguishing a nomination from an award decision keeps recognition meaningful and traceable.
familyMeaning.patents: Application records show a stage of intellectual-property activity. Clinical value needs its own evidence.
familyMeaning.marks-copyright: Product and publication identities help you locate the correct materials and distinguish ownership records from clinical evidence.
familyMeaning.whitebook: The Whitebook explains Pinnacle’s published framework and research narrative, which can guide more specific questions about sources.
familyMeaning.dossier: The dossier brings many institutional claims together; its value is strongest when each claim remains linked to its underlying record.
familyMeaning.september-handout: A dated company summary helps explain developments over time, including updates that supersede older publications.
familyMeaning.books: Parent resources can support informed conversations and everyday participation alongside an individual professional plan.
familyMeaning.sovereign-walkthrough: Helps you ask how the initial assessment, daily programme and monthly review connect. Ask the care team which version is used for your child and how recommendations are reviewed by people.

comparisonBoundary: Targeted review of five examples; no global exclusivity, dataset-size ranking, regulatory equivalence or comparative effectiveness established.
